items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: I remember hiring Lou Donaldson years ago for a series at a five star hotel... Twenty years later I’m doing the Clearwater Jazz Festival... he comes up to me.

ctx.x: And I started to realize, well why should I assume that these gentlemen have it made, that they don’t have to work anymore.

They don’t. You don’t. Sonny Rollins did a great interview, he says, “If you want to be a jazz musician” now he did very well, Sonny, but he’s saying, “Listen, you don’t do this for money. This is a spiritual thing” he says. So I mean I remember hiring Lou Donaldson years ago for a series at a five star hotel and I did a jazz series, and I hired Lou Donaldson, just one time. Twenty years later I’m doing the Clearwater Jazz Festival, on the bill, and Lou was on the bill. I’m backstage ready to go on and he comes…

“Lou that was twenty years ago.” So yeah, I told my press agent when I was in Europe, when I was only maybe 40 years old, this was before I joined Suzanne Somers, I said listen — and I’m not going to mention any names — I’m playing with these guys and I’m looking at them in their 70s and 80s doing one-nighters in Europe. And I said to him, he said, he reminds me. I remember what you said to me, I said I never want to end up like that.
